claim: A Juju (network) space is a logical grouping of subnets that can communicate with one another.
A space is used to help segment network traffic for the purpose of:
Spaces can be specified as constraints -- to determine what subnets a machine is connected to -- or as application endpoint bindings -- to determine the subnets used by application relations.
A binding associates an application endpoint with a space.
This restricts traffic for the endpoint to the subnets in the space.
By default, endpoints are bound to the space specified in the `default-space` model configuration value.
The name of the default space is "alpha".
Constraints and bindings affect application deployment and machine provisioning as well as the subnets a machine can talk to.
Endpoint bindings can be specified during deployment with `juju deploy --bind` or changed after deployment using the `juju bind` command.
Support for spaces may vary from one cloud to another.
For cloud-specific details, see the networking behavior section in each cloud's reference doc: Amazon EC2, Microsoft Azure, OpenStack, LXD, MAAS, Unmanaged.
